title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming stability & structured output
author: Claire Li
description: Motivation: bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer fully in parity with OpenAI semantics for params, roles, stop sequences, and logprobs while improving streaming stability and structured output formatting. This PR unifies request parameter parsing, normalizes role handling across system/user/assistant boundaries, implements correct stop token behavior for streaming and non-streaming flows, exposes token-level logprobs in parity with OpenAI responses, and fixes several streaming edge-cases that caused truncated events in high-concurrency workloads. Changes include backward-compatible API surface behavior, tests, and documentation updates. Checklist: - [x] API parameter parsing and validation - [x] Role normalization tests - [x] stop sequence handling for streaming and non-streaming - [x] token-level logprobs in responses and streaming deltas - [x] structured output formatting and de-escaping - [x] docs/quickstart update and changelog - [x] CI green. Related: Linear ENG-3421 (chat-parity), ENG-3540 (streaming-stability), PM-1183 (formatting-spec). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3421/openai-chat-completions-parity and internal RFC link: rfc/internal/2026/chat-completions-parity. Summary of approach: minimal layers added to compatibility adapter to translate incoming OpenAI-shaped requests into Redwood runtime calls, and to remap runtime responses and streaming events back to OpenAI-shaped deltas. For streaming stability we added event coalescing, per-connection backpressure awareness, and retry-safe idempotent end-of-stream markers. Non-goals: we do not change underlying model scoring or reranking logic in this PR. Tests: unit tests for param coercion and role mapping, integration tests for stop/logprobs formatting, and a canary job that exercises high-concurrency streaming. Migration notes: customers using the compatibility endpoint should see more faithful OpenAI-compatible outputs; no breaking changes expected.
commits: feat(adapter): map OpenAI params to runtime Config object and add validation for max_tokens/temperature/top_p/stop
fix(streaming): fix truncated streaming deltas by buffering partial tokens and coalescing small events
feat(logprobs): include token-level logprobs in streaming deltas and final response body following OpenAI schema
test: add end-to-end parity tests for roles and stop sequences (streaming + non-streaming)
docs: update /v1/chat.completions compatibility guide and release notes
review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you confirm behavior when stop tokens overlap with role separators? In particular we should ensure streaming deltas do not emit half-closed messages.

Claire Li: Added explicit role-separator trimming and test case in fixtures. streaming_coalescer now guarantees token-aligned deltas and emits an idempotent EOS marker. See tests/integration/test_chat_parity.py::test_stop_sequence_streaming.
Miguel Santos: The logprobs payload looks good, but ensure we cap size on streaming deltas to avoid huge memory spikes for long contexts.
Claire Li: Implemented a max-delta-bytes threshold with graceful flush; documented in streaming_coalescer and added canary.
release_notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for params, roles, stop/logprobs; improves streaming stability and structured output formatting. No breaking changes expected. See docs/api/openai_compat_chat.md for migration guidance.
summary: Compatibility adapter updates to achieve OpenAI chat.completions parity (params, roles, stop sequences, logprobs) plus streaming stability fixes and structured output formatting improvements.
notes: Canary passed against internal traffic mirror. Observability: added per-connection metrics (compat_stream_bytes, compat_stream_events, compat_stream_backpressure_seconds).
